title: `MIN` and `MAX` of floats: `-0.0` and `0.0` tie, and the last one read wins
verdict: the zeros compare equal; the sign of the result depends on the order of the rows
description: `min` and `max` of `FLOAT` and `DOUBLE` are the `float` and `double` instantiations of one template (`NumericMinMaxBase`). Each update is `Min::Operation(state, input)`, which for floats is `MinFloatingPoint`: a NaN is skipped, otherwise `right > left ? left : right`. When the state and the input compare equal, as `-0.0` and `0.0` do, the input replaces the state. `MaxFloatingPoint` is `left > right ? left : right` (a NaN wins), with the same rule for ties. Merging two partial states applies the same operation, the other state as the input.

So `MIN` over `0.0` and `-0.0` returns the zero read last, which depends on the order rows reach the aggregate and on how the parallel states merge. The sign is kept. A sort also treats the zeros as equal: `Radix::EncodeDouble` and `EncodeFloat` give both zeros the same key.
The group's `quantile_disc` and `median` were not read for this row.

Round 4 (probes): `min` and `max` of the rows 0.0, -0.0 are both `-0.0`, and of -0.0, 0.0 both `+0.0`, for DOUBLE and FLOAT: the zero read last wins. Over 1M rows the result was the last zero in table order at 1 and at 4 threads, in every run (10 to 20 each), so the merge order the source allows to vary did not show.
The docs are silent on which of two equal zeros `min` and `max` return: a docs gap. No upstream test pins this; it may change between versions.
reference: `zero_sign`: one zero (`ONE_ZERO`, #89). sverify's SQL makes `-0.0` into `0.0` on every read and after every operation that can make it (`Dialect.canon`, duckdb-R14), so `MIN` and `MAX` only meet `0.0`.

evidence.note: GetUnaryAggregate: FLOAT and DOUBLE instantiate the same template
NumericMinMaxBase: Execute and Combine call REDUCE_OP::Operation(state, input)

provenance.checked_by: characterization pipeline round 4 (probes; duckdb 2.0.0, Python, macOS arm64)

evidence.sql: CREATE TABLE z AS SELECT CASE WHEN i % 2 = 0 THEN '0.0' ELSE '-0.0' END::DOUBLE d, CASE WHEN i % 2 = 0 THEN '0.0' ELSE '-0.0' END::FLOAT f FROM range(1000000) r(i); SELECT signbit(min(d)), signbit(max(d)), signbit(min(f)), signbit(max(f)) FROM z
evidence.observed: true, true, true, true in 10 runs each at threads = 1 and threads = 4

evidence.sql: CREATE TABLE z AS SELECT CASE WHEN i < 500000 THEN '-0.0' ELSE '0.0' END::DOUBLE d, CASE WHEN i < 500000 THEN '-0.0' ELSE '0.0' END::FLOAT f FROM range(1000000) r(i); SELECT signbit(min(d)), signbit(max(d)), signbit(min(f)), signbit(max(f)) FROM z
evidence.observed: false, false, false, false in 20 runs each at threads = 1 and threads = 4, grouped or not

provenance.notes: `python -m sverify_dev.probe --observations --write` runs each query on a fresh connection under `TimeZone = 'UTC'` (or its own setup) and records the rows or the error as they come; `tests/test_probe.py::test_observations_are_current` checks they are current. The 1M-row runs are a scratch script outside the harness, since their result may vary.

evidence.note: min, max: silent on the sign of an equal zero; no upstream test either
